newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Moderna seen hurt in Q1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Moderna seen hurt in Q1.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Empresas La Moderna is seen reporting weak first quarter results due to lower prices in its high-margin cigarette business, analysts said.
A Reuters survey of three indusry analysts predicted first-quarter earnings per share of 0.59 centavos versus earnings per share of 1.25 pesos during the same quarter of 1996.
Analysts said comparisons between revenues and profits from year to year were not valid, however, because Moderna had sold some of its units during last year.
And part of the lower bottom line is due simply to lower monetary gains during the quarter, a non cash item, they said.
Divestitures of its grain seeds unit and part of its packaging division should make for lower revenues and operating profits, although it should eventually boost the company's margins, analysts said.
"You're going to see a noticeable drop in not only operating profits but also on the top line," Terry Sigler, an analyst at Robert Flemings in New York, told Reuters.
Sigler said the three main effects during the quarter would be the divestitures, lower cigarette prices and a seasonally slow quarter at the Seminis seed division.
La Moderna followed rival cigarette maker Cigatam, a unit of Grupo Carso, in lowering prices during the second half of the quarter in a bid to fight contraband cigarettes from the United States.

Analysts were divided on whether or not the operating margin at the company would rise or fall during the quarter. Lower cigarette prices are bound to hurt, but the divestitures allowed the company to focus on higher margin businesses.
But analysts agreed the second quarter should be better for the firm as its seed division turns in greater revenues and as cigarette prices recover.
"They are a more focused company and they should benefit from a recovery in Mexico this year," said Alyce Andrews, an analyst at Merrill Lynch in New York.
